title: Joining and Splitting NumPy Arrays
learningObjectives: Explain joining and splitting numpy arrays and its role in numerical Python.
Choose the appropriate NumPy operation for a given data task.
Predict array shapes, values and memory behavior before execution.
Write clear NumPy code and interpret its output.
Recognize common edge cases and validate assumptions.

understand.concept: NumPy provides concatenate and stack operations to combine arrays, plus split operations to divide arrays into sections. concatenate joins along an existing axis, while stack creates a new axis. The selected axis and input shapes must be compatible.
understand.whyItMatters: Joining and splitting are common when assembling batches, combining measurements and partitioning datasets for processing.
understand.analogy: Think of an array as a structured tray of values: its dimensions describe the compartments, and each operation determines whether values are shared, rearranged or selected.
understand.summary: NumPy provides concatenate and stack operations to combine arrays, plus split operations to divide arrays into sections. concatenate joins along an existing axis, while stack creates a new axis. The selected axis and input shapes must be compatible.

explain.narrative: Read the explanation, trace the dimensions and values, and run each example. The examples use deterministic inputs so their output can be checked exactly. NumPy provides concatenate and stack operations to combine arrays, plus split operations to divide arrays into sections. concatenate joins along an existing axis, while stack creates a new axis. The selected axis and input shapes must be compatible.

examples.title: Concatenate one-dimensional arrays
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1, 2])
b = np.array([3, 4])
print(np.concatenate((a, b)).tolist())
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates concatenate one-dimensional arrays using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Stack arrays as rows
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1, 2])
b = np.array([3, 4])
print(np.stack((a, b)).tolist())
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates stack arrays as rows using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Concatenate along columns
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([[1], [2]])
b = np.array([[3], [4]])
print(np.concatenate((a, b), axis=1).tolist())
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates concatenate along columns using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Split into equal sections
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
parts = np.split(a, 3)
print([p.tolist() for p in parts])
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates split into equal sections using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.

examples.title: Split a matrix by rows
examples.code:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6], [7, 8]])
parts = np.vsplit(a, 2)
print([p.shape for p in parts])
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates split a matrix by rows using the NumPy API and prints a deterministic result.
